facts: At each step, several candidate vectors (eight) are drawn from the generative head.
The targets are many vectors (one hundred) sampled from the autoencoder's Gaussian posterior for the true chunk, not a single target vector.
In the energy loss, the term comparing every model sample with every target sample is weighted by two.
In the energy loss, the term comparing every pair of different model samples is subtracted.
The distances are plain distances, not squared distances.
The loss is summed over the steps of the sequence.
Feeding the previous latent vector to the Transformer was tried and hurt performance.
The Transformer's input at each step is built from the previous chunk of K tokens, not from the previous latent vector.
A small two-layer MLP compresses the K token embeddings into a single input vector.
At inference, each predicted vector is decoded by the frozen autoencoder decoder into K tokens, which become the next step's input.
The encoder outputs the mean and standard deviation of a diagonal Gaussian, and the latent vector is sampled from it.
A KL divergence term pulls that Gaussian towards a standard normal prior.
The total loss is the reconstruction loss plus the KL term weighted by a small constant (zero point zero zero one).
The purpose is a smoother latent space, discouraging precise or large-magnitude latent values.
Some latent dimensions collapse to the standard normal prior and carry no information.
Collapsed dimensions inject noise that destabilises training of the downstream language model.
Each dimension's KL term is replaced by the larger of itself and a fixed floor, so pushing it below the floor gives no reward.
The floor is zero point five.
Dropout with a rate of fifteen percent is applied to the latent vector before the decoder.
Fifteen percent of the input tokens are masked, so the encoder must infer them from context.
Both kinds of dropout are used only while training the autoencoder, not while training or running the language model.
With these choices, four tokens map to a latent vector of one hundred and twenty eight dimensions.
For a temperature of one over an integer n, draw n samples and accept only if all n are identical; otherwise restart.
A general temperature is handled by splitting one over the temperature into an integer part and a fractional remainder.
The fractional part is handled by a Bernoulli factory procedure that simulates a coin whose success probability is the sample's probability raised to the remainder.
Failing at any stage restarts the whole process.
The whole image, as non-overlapping patches, goes through the target encoder.
The target blocks are taken from the target encoder's output, not from its input.
Four target blocks are sampled, each with a scale between fifteen and twenty percent and an aspect ratio between three quarters and one and a half.
Target blocks may overlap each other.
One context block is sampled with a scale between eighty five and one hundred percent and a square aspect ratio.
Any region of the context block that overlaps a target block is removed.
Only the remaining context patches are fed through the context encoder.
The predictor takes the context encoder's output plus one mask token per patch to be predicted.
Each mask token is one shared learnable vector with a positional embedding added.
The predictor is run once per target block, so four times.
